summary: Somerset County, MD, 120-ft CCC-era steel tower on Route 13 near Green Hill; register (2017) says removal was planned, association lists it gone, undated DNR report says standing.

facts.design: 120-foot steel tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
facts.status_note: Association list says 'Tower Gone' with no date; the 2017 register says DNR planned removal; a DNR report dated April 2007 lists the tower as standing; date of removal not found

events.note: State deed for the Green Hill site dated 19 September 1934; a July 13, 1934 item quoting the district forester named a planned Somerset County tower at Green Hill
Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as a 120-foot steel tower (register); a February 15, 1935 newspaper item called it new; DNR report gives installation date as unknown

DNR report dated April 2007: steel structure in good shape, wooden steps and cab in bad condition, first 20 feet of steps removed, fenced compound overgrown; recommends consideration as a future communications site
Registered August 23, 2017 as US 1235, MD 8; the register says DNR planned to remove the tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The association list says Tower Gone with no date. The 2017 register says DNR planned removal. The DNR report dated April 2007 lists the tower as present. Recorded as gone with the conflict stated in status_note, because no dated source confirms removal and the removal date is not found.
The register gives 1935 and a February 1935 newspaper item describes the tower as new. The DNR report gives the installation date as unknown. Recorded as 1935.

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties Report

notes_for_editor: Build history is well sourced. The status 'gone' rests on one undated association listing. The 2017 register says removal was planned, and the DNR report dated April 2007 shows the tower standing, so the editor should confirm the status before publishing. An undated newspaper item grouped with the 1934 items gave a planned 130-foot height; the register and the February 15, 1935 item say 120 feet, which the record uses. The NHLR page carries a DNR photo credit with no image URL, so no photo record was added. No staffing, fire or access records were found; access level is omitted. The register's 'Maryland DNR history' link is a separate PDF hosted by the register (nhlr.org/media/3287/...), not the DNR report cited here; it was not read. The brief's record matches the NHLR page (height, elevation, registration date, agency), so no corrections were made.
